title: Toni's Spreadsheet
teaser: Toni Treasure color-codes everything. One spreadsheet, five tabs, every timestamp.

news.headline: Tab One: Manifest
news.body: A spreadsheet called "TONI 2026 ✨ (do not share)" is landing in Lola's inbox one tab at a time. Tab one is a vision board in cells, and it's very ambitious.
news.post:
Roommates, a little birdie with a nail file sent me something today, and I've been staring at it for three hours like it's the menu at a new restaurant.

It's a spreadsheet. The file name is "TONI 2026 ✨ (do not share)." Somebody shared it. My source says it lives in a group chat Toni Treasure uses for her hair, nails and lash appointments, and she only ever shares one tab at a time. So that's how I'm getting it, y'all: one tab at a time, a slow drip of chaos.

Tab one is called "MANIFEST." It's a vision board, but in cells. Sis color-codes her dreams: green means done, yellow means in progress, pink means "secured." Let me read you some rows.

Row 2: "Move out of Whitestone." Yellow. Row 3: "400K followers." Green, with a checkmark she must have added this morning, because, babe, she hit that number by breakfast. Row 4: "Learn to read contracts." Green. Underlined twice. Row 5: "Debut single by Halloween." Yellow. Row 6: "Never pay for dinner again." Green. Row 7: "Two investors." Pink. With a little heart.

Two investors, Roommates. Now, I'm not saying anything. I'm just saying that yesterday two of the biggest rappers in New York posted her in the same booth fifty minutes apart, and today I'm looking at a cell that says "Two investors 💕." The internet would call that a coincidence. I call it Thursday.

There's a column on the far right called "Notes," and most of it is cute. "Drink water." "Ring light needs a new bulb." "Stop saying 'literally' on camera." And then, in row 9, a note with no task next to it at all: "Same booth. Same dress. Different nights. Trust the process."

Not sis turning a corner booth into a business plan. I don't know what the process is yet, and I deadass mean that. But I know a woman with a plan when I see one, and I respect a spreadsheet with conditional formatting. That's not a vision board, that's aura.

My inbox is already wildin'. Half of y'all think "two investors" means a manager and a stylist. The other half have opened spreadsheets of your own.

My source says the next tab is called "BUDGET," and that it's "very, very specific."

So tell me, Roommates: what would be in row 1 of your manifest tab? And who do you think the two investors are?

news.headline: Tab Two: Budget
news.body: The budget tab is here, and Toni tracks everything down to the napkin. Literally the napkin.
news.post:
Roommates, tab two came in this morning, and I need to start by saying I have never been this impressed by a woman's relationship with money.

The tab is called "BUDGET," and it has four columns: "Item," "Cost," "Who paid" and "Value." Not value like price. Value like what she expects to get out of it. Chile, that's a whole different kind of math.

The highlights. "Red dress, dry cleaning × 2." Who paid: "investor." Value: "400K." "Rooftop dinner." Who paid: "investor." Next row, "Rooftop dinner," the very next night. Who paid: "other investor." Value, both nights: "content." "Car home." Who paid: "investor (didn't know)." "Ring light bulb." Who paid: "me 😤." Value: "everything." "Regular coffee from the cart." Cost: C$2. Who paid: "me." Value: "humility."

Then line 14, the one keeping me up at night. "Napkins (Sal's) × 2." Cost: C$0. Who paid: "free." Value: "TBD." Bold. Highlighted pink.

Napkins, y'all. Two napkins from Ditmars Deli & Dreams, the same deli Lord Menace is suing over a chalkboard sandwich, and she put them in her budget with a pink highlight and the word "TBD." What is the value of a napkin? Who budgets a napkin? Sal hands those out by the fistful. I asked him, and he said, "Mira, napkins are free," and went back to slicing.

At the bottom there's a little section called "Never Again," and it's just a list: "splitting the check," "paying for parking," "men who say 'I'll get the next one.'" Sis has boundaries, and they are documented.

My favorite part is the running total in the corner. It's not money spent. It's money "saved," the cell is labeled "MY FUTURE 💅," and the number goes up every day.

Is any of this illegal? No. Is it a little grimy? A little. Is it a flex? Facts. A lot of y'all keep calling Toni a sweet girl caught in the middle. I'm not saying she isn't. I'm saying sweet girls don't usually have a "Value" column.

The next tab, according to my source, is "GIFTS." She says it has two of everything.

So tell me, Roommates: what do you think a napkin is worth? And would you ever let somebody else pay for your ring light?

news.headline: Tab Three: Gifts
news.body: The gifts tab has two of everything: two bouquets, two giant teddy bears, two diamond phone cases. Every row has a column called "Keep?"
news.hook: There's one more tab, locked, called "CALENDAR." My source can't open it. Yet.
news.post:
Roommates, I watched this woman cry on the radio this morning, one tear, left eye, perfectly lit. Then my source sent me tab three, and now I need you to look at it with me.

The tab is called "GIFTS." Columns: "Item," "From," "Return value," "Keep?"

Row 1: "Roses, 2 dozen." From: "M." Keep: "photo first." Row 2: "Roses, 2 dozen." From: "R." Keep: "photo first." Row 3: "Teddy bear, 4 ft." From: "M." Keep: "no. scary." Row 4: "Teddy bear, 4 ft." From: "R." Keep: "no. scarier." Row 5: "Diamond phone case." From: "M." Return value: "C$40,000." Keep: "no ✔ returned." Row 6: "Diamond phone case." From: "R." Return value: "C$40,000." Keep: "not yet."

Y'all. The jeweler told me one case came back for cash the same afternoon. Here it is, in a cell, with a checkmark. And the other one says "not yet." Not "no." Not "never." "Not yet." Sis is pacing her returns. M and R. I wonder who those could be. I'll wait.

There's a second section on the same tab called "RADIO," and I'm reading it exactly as written, because I'm still processing: "Wear white. Sunglasses inside. Bring own ring light (they won't have one). Cry at min 12, left eye only (better side). Say 'different ways, different days.' Say 'respect my privacy.' Read tip link twice."

Chile. CHILE. The tear was scheduled. Minute twelve, left eye, "better side." I went back to the clip, and the tear drops at 12:03. That's not a breakdown, that's a run of show. Plus a thousand aura for the planning, minus a thousand for the teddy bears.

My inbox is in shambles. Some of y'all are tight that the tear was fake. Some of y'all are taking notes for your next breakup. I'm not judging, B. I once cried on cue over a parking ticket.

Now here's what's bugging me. At the end of the tab list there's one more tab with a padlock emoji, called "CALENDAR." My source can't open it. She says Toni has shared every other tab with that group chat at least once, but never that one.

What's on a calendar that you lock, Roommates? Who are you hiding your schedule from? And be honest: would you have kept the phone case?

news.headline: Tab Four: Calendar
news.body: The locked tab finally opened. It's Toni's calendar: two pedicures booked by "a friend," a rooftop photo shot a week early and a dental emergency that never happened.
news.hook: One entry every few days, with no detail at all: "Post 🧾."
news.post:
Roommates, the padlock came off. Last night, after two rappers walked out of one restroom on the Ditmars Heights Rooftop with forty-eight roses between them, my source finally got into the tab called "CALENDAR." I've been reading it since 2 AM.

I'll go in order. A Tuesday, 11:00: "Talon Talk × 2. Book as 'a friend.' Curtain closed. Bring cucumbers (they never have enough)."

Y'all. The pedicures. In the margin of the spa's appointment book, the receptionist wrote "she says they'll love the surprise." Here's the she. Here's the surprise. Here are the cucumbers.

Same week: "Call Desmond's mom's office: 'when's his next cleaning?' (cute voice)." A few days later: "Gerald: find the oboe case. Under the bed. It's always under the bed."

Then: "Grandma molar: tell M Monday, tell R Wednesday. 8 + 8. (Grandma has dentures, don't mention.)" Roommates, she wrote "don't mention." She wrote it down so she wouldn't mention it. That's discipline.

Then: "Rooftop, table by the railing. Take date-night photo. Post NEXT week, 9 PM." So the "date night tomorrow 💕" post that sent both men running into one restroom was shot a week early, like a magazine cover.

And sprinkled through the whole tab, every few days, sometimes twice a day, one entry with no detail at all: "Post 🧾." I lined the dates up with every @QueensReceipts drop. The tow receipt. The robes. The dental reminder. The oboe memo at 1 AM. Every "Post 🧾" lands a few minutes before the account posted.

Now, I'm not going to say it. The main story says it tomorrow, and I have manners. But I've read a lot of calendars in my life, and this is the first one that made me put my phone face down and go get a chopped cheese to calm down.

Is it grimy? Odee grimy. Is it also the most organized thing I've ever seen in Queens? Facts.

My source says there's one last tab, the very first one Toni made, called "TOTALS." She says it's "the whole thing."

So tell me, Roommates: if you found your own name in somebody's calendar like this, would you be mad, or impressed?

news.headline: The Whole Sheet
news.body: Every tab, every total and the tab Toni made first. Her C$310,000, the napkins' real value and a brand-new tab called "PHASE 2."
news.hook: PHASE 2 has one row so far: "Brooklyn. Two producers. Same booth."
news.post:
Roommates, it's done, and so is the spreadsheet. Toni Treasure dropped "Both of Y'all" on the Big Screen last night, and an hour later she shared the whole file, every tab, captioned "for the girls who take notes 📊." The file name never changed: "TONI 2026 ✨ (do not share)." Sis shared it with everybody.

The first tab she ever made is called "TOTALS," and it's beautiful. Rooftop dinners: C$94,000. Studio budget: C$60,000 from M, C$60,000 from R. Grandma's molar: C$16,000. Phone cases, both returned: C$80,000. Grand total, in a gold cell: C$310,000. Next to it: "Tips not included. I'm not a monster."

Remember line 14 of the budget? "Napkins (Sal's) × 2. Value: TBD." It's filled in now. Value: "50% of everything." With photos of both napkins: Desmond Pettibone's signature and Gerald Fennimore III's, each under "Toni gets 50% of anything that comes out of this, beef included," and "Sal" as witness on both. Half of number two on the Queens chart and half of number three are hers. Number one is all hers.

The manifest tab got updated too. "Debut single by Halloween": green, a day early. "Two investors": now marked "returned." "Learn to read contracts": green, with a note: "Lawyers offered to represent me. Lol."

There's a tab I'd never seen, called "THANK YOU." It's short. "Sal: witnessed, never asked questions. Send a fruit basket." "Talon Talk: the cucumbers. Big tip." "Sharm: sorry about the subpoenas. Sending a ring light." "Nour: the 9 PM slot. I owe you koshari." I'm not crying. You're crying.

And then the last tab: "PHASE 2." One row so far: "Brooklyn. Two producers. Same booth. Different nights." Status: yellow. In progress.

The internet is in shambles, and honestly, so is my own budget. One woman ran two rappers, two lawyers, one deli, one spa and the whole Queens chart from a color-coded sheet with a sparkle emoji in the file name. We love to see a plan come together, even when it's grimy. Wepa.

So tell me, Roommates: would you open a tab called PHASE 2? And if Toni ever hands you a napkin, do you sign it, or run?
